# Labels below follow the Rhode Island Hospital Discharge Data dictionary
# (HDD2015-18cy6-20-19, revised 6/20/2019). Unknown codes stay visible.
label_from_dictionary <- function(x, codebook, field) {
  code <- trimws(as.character(x))
  key <- toupper(code)
  numeric_code <- !is.na(code) & grepl("^[0-9]+$", code)
  key[numeric_code] <- as.character(as.integer(code[numeric_code]))
  label <- unname(codebook[key])
  missing <- is.na(code) | code == "" | code %in% c(".A", ".")
  unknown <- !missing & is.na(label)
  label[missing] <- "Missing / unknown"
  label[unknown] <- paste0("Not listed in data dictionary (", field, " code ", code[unknown], ")")
  label
}

labelled_factor <- function(x, codebook, field) {
  labels <- label_from_dictionary(x, codebook, field)
  levels <- unique(c(unname(codebook), setdiff(unique(labels), unname(codebook))))
  factor(labels, levels = levels)
}

## Q7 - Refer to the data description in the file HDD2015-18cy6-20-19.docx, which variable recording the month of admission?, which variable recording the month of discharge?
##According to the Rhode Island Department of Health documentation (pages 6–7), moa represents the month of admission, and mod represents the month of discharge. Both variables use values from 1 to 12 to represent January through December.
## Q8- Which month admitted the most number of patients? Which month admitted the most number of male patients?
dfN %>%
  group_by(moa_label) %>%
  summarise(patients = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(patients))

dfN %>%
  filter(sex == 1) %>%
  group_by(moa_label) %>%
  summarise(patients = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(patients))
##Q9 - Which month has the most number of teenage female patients?
dfN %>%
  filter(sex == 2, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>%
  group_by(moa_label) %>%
  summarise(patients = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(patients))
## Q10. Which provider had the most female patients in October?
dfN %>%
  filter(sex == 2, moa == 10) %>%
  group_by(provider_label) %>%
  summarise(patients = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(patients))
## Q11. Are female patients older than male patients on average?
dfN %>%
  group_by(sex_label) %>%
  summarise(avg_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE))
## Q12. Calculate average age by month. Which month has the oldest patients?
dfN %>%
  group_by(moa_label) %>%
  summarise(avg_age = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_age))
## Q13. Which provider has the highest total charge?
dfN %>%
  group_by(provider_label) %>%
  summarise(total_charge = sum(tot, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_charge))
## Q14. Which provider has the lowest average total charge for teenage males?
dfN %>%
  filter(sex == 1, age >= 13, age <= 19) %>%
  group_by(provider_label) %>%
  summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(avg_charge)
## Q15. Create a season variable and calculate average length of stay.
dfN <- dfN %>%
  mutate(season = case_when(
    moa %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
    moa %in% c(3, 4, 5) ~ "Spring",
    moa %in% c(6, 7, 8) ~ "Summer",
    moa %in% c(9, 10, 11) ~ "Fall"
  ))

dfN %>%
  group_by(season) %>%
  summarise(avg_los = mean(los, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_los))
## Q16. Average charge for a 20-year-old male staying one day in Fall.
dfN %>%
  filter(
    age == 20,
    sex == 1,
    los == 1,
    season == "Fall"
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    avg_charge = mean(tot, na.rm = TRUE),
    patients = n()
  )

Part 2 — Data Visualization

Plot 1 — Age Distribution

ggplot(dfN, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5,
                 fill = "steelblue",
                 color = "white",
                 na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution of Hospital Patients",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 2 — Patients by Sex

dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sex_label)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Hospital Patients by Sex",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 3 — Hospital Admissions by Type

dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(admtype)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = admtype_label)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Hospital Admissions by Type",
       x = "Admission Type",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 4 — Average Length of Stay by Age Group

dfN %>%
  mutate(age_group = cut(age,
                         breaks = c(0, 18, 40, 65, Inf),
                         labels = c("0-18", "19-40",
                                    "41-65", "66+"),
                         include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(avg_stay = mean(los, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = avg_stay)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Average Hospital Stay by Age Group",
       x = "Age Group",
       y = "Average Days in Hospital") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 5 — Average Patient Charges by Hospital

dfN %>%
  group_by(provider_label) %>%
  summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(provider_label, avg_charge),
             y = avg_charge)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Average Patient Charges by Hospital",
       x = "Hospital",
       y = "Average Charge ($)") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 6 — Hospital Charges vs. Length of Stay

dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(los), !is.na(tot),
         los >= 0, tot > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = los, y = tot)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Hospital Charges vs. Length of Stay",
       x = "Length of Stay (Days)",
       y = "Total Charges ($, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()

Plot 7 — Hospital Charges by Service Category

dfN %>%
  mutate(across(c(trandb, orr, lab, phar, dtest, ther),
                as.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(
    Room_Board = sum(trandb, na.rm = TRUE),
    Operating_Room = sum(orr, na.rm = TRUE),
    Laboratory = sum(lab, na.rm = TRUE),
    Pharmacy = sum(phar, na.rm = TRUE),
    Diagnostic_Tests = sum(dtest, na.rm = TRUE),

  pivot_longer(everything(),

  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(category, charges),

  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Hospital Charges by Service Category",
       x = "Service Category",
       y = "Total Charges ($)") +
  theme_minimal()

library(gganimate)

df2 <- dfN %>%

Part 3

Setup

library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)

set.seed(123)

Question 1

# Select variables and remove missing values
df3 <- dfN %>%
  select(tot, age, sex, raceethn, provider, moa,
         mod, admtype, campus, los) %>%
  filter(raceethn != "", admtype != "") %>%
  mutate(
    age = as.numeric(age),
    los = as.numeric(los),
    tot = as.numeric(tot)
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

# Create target
med <- median(df3$tot)

df3 <- df3 %>%
  mutate(target = factor(ifelse(tot < med, "low", "high"))) %>%
  select(-tot)

# Convert categorical variables to factors
df3 <- df3 %>%
  mutate(across(c(sex, raceethn, provider, moa,
                  mod, admtype, campus), as.factor))

# Training 10%, Testing 90%
set.seed(123)

index <- createDataPartition(df3$target, p = 0.10, list = FALSE)

train1 <- df3[index, ]
test1 <- df3[-index, ]

nrow(train1)
## [1] 12754
nrow(test1)
## [1] 114773
table(train1$target)
## 
## high  low 
## 6377 6377

Question 2

# Decision tree
tree1 <- rpart(target ~ ., data = train1,
               method = "class",
               control = rpart.control(minsplit = 2, cp = 0.001))

rpart.plot(tree1)

          horiz = TRUE,

          col = "steelblue",
          main = "Variable Importance")

Question 6 — Second Target

Predict whether a patient has a short or long hospital stay.

# Select variables and remove missing values
df4 <- dfN %>%
  select(los, age, sex, raceethn, provider,
         moa, mod, admtype, campus) %>%
  filter(raceethn != "", admtype != "") %>%
  mutate(
    age = as.numeric(age),
    los = as.numeric(los)
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

# Create target
med2 <- median(df4$los)

df4 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(target = factor(ifelse(los > med2, "long", "short"))) %>%
  select(-los)

# Convert categorical variables
df4 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(across(c(sex, raceethn, provider, moa,
                  mod, admtype, campus), as.factor))

# Training 10%, Testing 90%
set.seed(123)

index2 <- createDataPartition(df4$target, p = 0.10, list = FALSE)

train2 <- df4[index2, ]
test2 <- df4[-index2, ]

nrow(train2)
## [1] 12753
nrow(test2)
## [1] 114774
table(train2$target)
## 
##  long short 
##  5441  7312
